requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
## Judgment

The sources satisfy `requirements.references.outline_comments`. The `{impl}` marking is complete and the tests cover the design space. I found no gaps, and there are no FIXME acknowledgements.

## Implementation

**Profiles define comments.**
- `Profile.is_comment` (`src/outline/profile.rs`) is set per profile.
- Rust uses `line_comment` and `block_comment`.
- CSS uses `comment` or `js_comment`.
- Python, TOML, TypeScript/TSX and YAML use the shared `kind_is_comment`.
- Markdown uses `src/outline/markdown.rs::is_comment`, which accepts only `html_block` nodes that start with `<!--` and end with `-->`. An inline HTML comment is therefore never a comment and stays paragraph text of its section.

**Runs.**
- `assign_comments` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) joins comments into one run only when four conditions hold:
  - neither comment follows code on its line (`trails_code`);
  - the gap between them is whitespace only;
  - the next comment starts on the previous comment's end line or the line after;
  - both have the same container-binding.
- A comment that follows code, including one that follows another comment on the same line, therefore forms a run alone.
- Trailing runs go to `trailing_owner`, which descends to the innermost node whose line range covers the line.
- Other runs go to `run_owner`. It finds the smallest node containing the run and returns the first child starting after the run, or the container itself (the root at top level) when there is none.

**Container binding.**
- `comment_binds_to_container` is wired through `DraftComment` and `record_comment`.
- Rust sets it to `is_inner_doc_comment` (`//!`, `/*!`). Every other profile sets it to `never`.
- `run_owner` returns the smallest containing node for such runs, so a file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root.
- Because the binding flag is part of the join condition, an adjacent `//!` line and `//` line form separate runs. A strict reading of the first sentence ("consecutive lines … MUST form one comment run") could object. The requirement's own "such a run" wording and the container-binding rule need this split, and the tests assert it for `mod m { //! Module docs. // above inner fn inner() }`.

**References count for the owning node.**
- `Outline::owner_at_line` returns the comment owner on the line, otherwise the smallest innermost node covering it.
- It is used by `reference_selector` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`), `citation_items` (`src/citations.rs`) and `reference_set_digest` (`src/evidence.rs`).
- `comment_fences` (`src/fenced.rs`) carries each run's owner into `SourceFence.owner`. `src/rust_coverage.rs` consumes it under `rust_item_coverage`, which is named in the requirement and carries its own `{impl}`.
- Every function that implements part of the rule is marked `{impl}` for this requirement: the profile statics, `Profile`, the comment helpers, `assign_comments`, `trailing_owner`, `run_owner`, `content_end`, the `Outline` query methods and the consumers listed above.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs::references` also calls `owner_at_line`, but only to report an item. It is not marked for this requirement. I did not count that as a gap: the requirement's reference-counting sentence names only `rust_item_coverage` and `authoring_inputs`, and `reference_index` carries its own `{cite}` of this requirement for the owner selector it reports.

## Tests

The `{test}` references are in `src/outline/tests.rs`, `src/fenced.rs`, `src/evidence.rs`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs` and `src/authoring/tools.rs`. They cover these cases:

- **Next-node, container and root ownership:** `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container`, `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next`, `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root`. Together they cover a run before a node, a run after the container's last node, the root at top level, and blank-line separation of runs.
- **Trailing comments:** `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` and `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` (`/* first */ /* second */` gives the root).
- **Inner doc comments:** `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root`, for `//!` and `/*!`, plus the `//!`-in-`mod` case above.
- **Every language:** `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` runs Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown through the same rules. The YAML-specific tests (`yaml_comments_before_a_key…` and `workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows`) cover the `trailing_comments_outside` quirk.
- **Markdown:** `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` asserts that an inline HTML comment is not a comment and is text of its section.
- **References counting for the owning node:** `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node` and `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes`, plus `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run` for run-scoped fences and owners.

The tests cover the interesting boundaries and the failure-adjacent cases (unclosed fence in a separate run, comment with nothing after it).

{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and

:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
